source.note: Counts below are source decoder invocations, not independent hypotheses or unique keystreams.

known_overlap: The existing 32-case raw-payload pilot is already contained in the Part 1 main grid and in Part 2a masks 0 and 63.
All 120 shift=0 raw-payload configurations in Part 1b duplicate Part 1 main configurations at offset zero. The two witness-corner masks contribute those same 120 cases to Part 2a.

Part 2b's six majority-value rows per generator collapse to one seed, leaving 90 repeated decoder invocations within that part. Its six single-witness-alternative seeds per generator also occur in Part 2a, though Part 2a additionally tests both reductions and signs.

For Part 2a specifically, hashing the full 1,664-symbol effective screen key gives 2,596 unique key/sign cases among 3,840 invocations: AES-128-CTR ignores all six contested positions, while four AES-256/ChaCha variants use only position 25. This 1,244-case reduction is measured, not inferred solely from source labels.
Other algebraic or keystream equivalences across Part 1, shifts, and Part 2b are possible; no exhaustive global unique-output count has been claimed.

timing_probe.qualification: Measured on this host on 2026-10-22 using two complete contested-byte masks. The full grid also generates longer keystreams and full-page reruns, so its wall time is likely higher.

execution_decision: Replay the complete 3,840-case Part 2a as one bounded record. Defer the full ~70,680-invocation replay until a long-running batch is justified. Do not equate a partial screen with validation of the source's full negative claim.
reusable_efficiency: Generate each PRF stream once per seed/generator/reduction, hash the effective screen key, decode each unique key/sign pair once, and fan the exact score back to its source-defined case rows. Preserve source order, beam and scorer; validate the shortcut against an unchanged source sample and run controls first. Keep published source runs separate from any deduplicated computational shortcut.
